# Current core feature inventory

Source review: **2026-10-05**. Core baseline: `1f7c96d4deb6f1b64fd3a4be5b18e5a29d608242`; Rust baseline: `0a2a68a783dda8ed00adb15c9456646783e05893`.

This is the existing core capability inventory. Rust notes describe inspected implementation sources, not the draft Rust specification or a live parity certificate. Both repositories can change during rollout; these baseline revisions identify the review window, not a pinned running binary.

**259 capability records**, **92/92 feature directories referenced**, **30 declared kernel skills**, **176 numbered ADR files**. Counts are generated from source and curated records. A referenced directory is coverage of that subsystem, not proof that every function or user journey has passed.

Core classifications: gated: 49; implemented: 29; partial: 6; retired: 1; wired: 174.

Evidence states: **wired** = a caller/boot/package path uses the implementation; **implemented** = a concrete exported implementation exists; **gated** = configuration, consent, credentials or activation controls availability; **partial** = the named contract is incomplete or narrower; **retired** = compatibility remains but deliberately refuses execution. Existing test references are acceptance entry points; they were not rerun as part of this source inventory.

Rust **not-located** means the equivalent was not found in the bounded inspected sources; **not-reviewed** means no individual mapping was attempted. Neither means proven absence. A Rust **wired** entry is not a full equivalence verdict.

Boundaries: **platform** is the control plane; **shared-engine** is reusable package-facing functionality retained in core; **node** is worker/device execution; **package-boundary** is hosting and SDK behavior; **resident-application** is an application deliberately retained in this repository. An application screen or a catalog registration does not by itself establish its backend.

The Rust builder subsequently reported remediation of the preliminary RK findings. That report is separate from this feature inventory and requires independent deployed-build revalidation; its certification language is not adopted here.

## How the provider, harness and tool contracts fit

- **Inference/model provider:** `LLMService` and provider resolution select the model, credentials and completion port (MODEL records).
- **Agent harness:** `HarnessAdapter`, `HarnessTask` and `HarnessResult` select an agent runtime and execution policy (HARNESS records).
- **Tools/connectors:** tool registry, switches, selectors and execution bridges control callable operations; connector adapters supply scoped provider access (TOOL/CONN records).
- Persona composition, layered bot brains and capability-provider selection are additional contracts. “Layer” also names FSD imports and prompt sections; these are not interchangeable three-layer APIs. See [the architecture layer glossary](./README.md#layer-means-five-different-things-in-this-codebase).

| [SEC-06: Durable protected remote and inline result authority](#sec-06) | Remote permit lifecycle and controller-only startInline/completeInline share durable authority, current owner/policy/snapshot checks and original ceilings. Empty admission requires zero actual messages and current ownership; nonempty no-lineage history remains refused. Inline records are controller provenance, not forged signed worker permits. Current registrations mint a random generation at each API boot, and assertSnapshot requires exact generation equality; prior protected answers are therefore fenced after restart. Stable release identity for durable history remains incomplete. |
| [TOOL-12: Workflow Studio agent-tool HTTP translation contract](#tool-12) | ToolExecutorService constructs the integration for the local /api/workflow-studio base URL and dispatches the workflow-studio tool. The integration implements get/post/put and all named actions, while target routes are mounted with requiresAuth. Reviewed fetch calls carry no forwarded caller authorization/session headers, so successful authorization across this agent-tool-to-local-API boundary is not established from the implementation; mark partial rather than count the HTTP client as a working authenticated workflow author. Existing mounted server routes belong to the Workflow Studio capability; this integration itself mounts no new route. |
| [DATA-12: Personal knowledge graph and connector ingestion](#data-12) | PERSONAL_GRAPH_ROUTES=on enables operator-only read/ingest mounts using one shared InMemoryGraphStore. The owner-qualified PostgresGraphStore is implemented but is not that mounted store; ordinary user graph HTTP access is not established. |

<a id="auth-01"></a>
### AUTH-01 — Verified principal directory and issuer identity

Resolve people by verified issuer and exact subject, with explicit directory registration and historical references. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Protocol claims take precedence over presentation-filtered OIDC user data. The auth probe exposes principalIssuer; invalid present protocol evidence does not fall back to a guessed issuer. Registration does not simulate a verified sign-in.

User operations: Inspect a scoped user roster; Register known identities for access review; Keep identical subjects from different issuers separate.

Core evidence: [src/shared/middleware/principal-issuer.ts](../../src/shared/middleware/principal-issuer.ts), [src/app/routes/auth-state-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/auth-state-routes.ts), [src/app/composition/application-principal-directory.ts](../../src/app/composition/application-principal-directory.ts), [src/features/principal-directory/store.ts](../../src/features/principal-directory/store.ts), [src/features/principal-directory/registration-store.ts](../../src/features/principal-directory/registration-store.ts), [src/app/routes/user-directory-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/user-directory-routes.ts).

Rust: **partial**. OIDC links use issuer+subject and durable principal IDs. At this source snapshot kernel.rs has removed its synthetic-token shortcut and auth_user refuses anonymous introspection, but the compatibility response still substitutes internal principal ID into user.sub and omits verified issuer; deployed remediation was not rechecked. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/identity/src/oidc.rs`, `crates/people/src/providers.rs`, `crates/control/src/kernel.rs`, `crates/api/src/ui_api.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/auth/user`, `/api/user-directory`, `/api/user-directory/preview`, `/api/user-directory/apply`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/149-enterprise-application-authorization.md](../../docs/adr/149-enterprise-application-authorization.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/auth-state-principal-issuer.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/auth-state-principal-issuer.spec.ts), [tests/unit/principal-directory.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/principal-directory.spec.ts), [tests/unit/principal-registration.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/principal-registration.spec.ts).

### AUTH-03 — Invited local user accounts

Provide controlled password login when an external identity provider is unavailable or alongside a hybrid deployment. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** The local store uses scrypt password hashes and hashed one-time invitation/reset tokens. User operations: Invite an account by email; Accept an expiring single-use invitation; Sign in with a local password.

The core local login page/API contract is not reproduced by those different HTTP surfaces. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/oshald/src/local_accounts.rs`, `crates/people/src/invitations.rs`, `crates/api/src/people.rs`, `crates/api/src/sessions_api.rs`.

<a id="auth-04"></a>
### AUTH-04 — Local session lifetime and revocation

Keep local sessions signed, bounded in lifetime and checked against current account state. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Local cookies have a rolling 24-hour and absolute seven-day ceiling; session snapshots and versions prevent disabled accounts or superseded credentials retaining access.

User operations: Remain signed in within the rolling window; End the session by signing out; Lose session access when the account is disabled.

Core evidence: [src/features/local-auth/services/local-auth-session.ts](../../src/features/local-auth/services/local-auth-session.ts), [src/features/local-auth/services/local-user-store.ts](../../src/features/local-auth/services/local-user-store.ts), [src/app/routes/local-auth-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/local-auth-routes.ts).

Rust: **wired**. SessionStore persists digests, applies absolute/idle timeout, supports per-principal revocation, and is attached to local and OIDC sources. This is an equivalent lifecycle with a different cookie/store implementation. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/identity/src/session.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/local_accounts.rs`, `crates/api/src/sessions_api.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Core route references: `/logout`, `/api/local-auth/login`, `/api/local-auth/state`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/117-local-auth-invited-users.md](../../docs/adr/117-local-auth-invited-users.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/local-auth-session.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/local-auth-session.spec.ts), [tests/unit/local-auth-middleware.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/local-auth-middleware.spec.ts).

<a id="auth-09"></a>
### AUTH-09 — Installer root election and transfer

Establish one recovery owner at installation and transfer that ownership through explicit authority. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Installer setup locks and validates an empty installation, origin and elected verified identity. Swarm roles refuse root removal and transfer atomically to the next owner.

User operations: Complete a bound installer setup; Claim root on an empty installation; Transfer root without leaving the installation ownerless.

Core evidence: [src/app/composition/installer-root-bootstrap.ts](../../src/app/composition/installer-root-bootstrap.ts), [src/features/swarm-roles/services/swarm-role-store.ts](../../src/features/swarm-roles/services/swarm-role-store.ts), [src/app/routes/swarm-roles-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/swarm-roles-routes.ts).

Rust: **wired**. Kernel uses a fixed invariant root row, confirmed transfer and immutable root-removal refusal; daemon reconciles configured credentials to the durable owner. Core browser installer proof/origin flow differs. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/control/src/kernel.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/swarm/roles/status`, `/api/swarm/roles/claim-root`, `/api/swarm/roles/installer-root`, `/api/swarm/roles/transfer-root`, `/api/local-auth/bootstrap`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/148-swarm-root.md](../../docs/adr/148-swarm-root.md).

<a id="auth-11"></a>
### AUTH-11 — Business tenants and explicit memberships

Organize businesses or other groups with explicit active membership and membership roles. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Tenant routes and connector-tenancy store require current membership/admin semantics for members and connection visibility. Business membership is explicit, not inherited merely from login-provider directory membership.

User operations: Create a tenant; List own tenants; Add or remove a tenant member; Manage tenant membership roles.

Core evidence: [src/app/routes/tenant-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/tenant-routes.ts), [src/app/routes/connector-tenancy.ts](../../src/app/routes/connector-tenancy.ts), [src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts](../../src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Tenants library and HTTP member routes exist, but kernel admission currently confines a non-root caller to its principal.tenant rather than consulting active memberships for header selection. Root can choose arbitrary tenant scope; core membership-aware business authorization is not established by tenant storage alone. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/people/src/tenants.rs`, `crates/api/src/tenants_api.rs`, `crates/control/src/kernel.rs`, `crates/api/src/extract.rs`.

Grant external verified people explicit business membership without copying identity-provider tenancy into business data. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** The external membership authority resolves exact issuer+subject and refreshes actor/target before atomically applying a reviewed change.

<a id="auth-13"></a>

Use trusted directory evidence and an opt-in Entra migration bridge without replacing canonical local identity. **Core: gated; boundary: platform.** Bridge is opt-in, tenant-bound and rejects invalid configuration. Protocol evidence is retained separately from filtered user data, kept fresh and evaluated against issuer+directory tenant group mappings.

<a id="auth-14"></a>
### AUTH-14 — Application tiers, named roles and data permission scopes

Enforce application-owned permissions, scopes and fields within a coarse application access ceiling. **Core: wired; boundary: package-boundary.** Current registration binds catalog/source revisions; exact roles and permission denials resolve centrally. Runtime mounts and operation adapters enforce declared bot/tool/route policies. Package data adapters remain responsible for authoritative own/team/tenant and field enforcement; engine support is not proof every package declares a complete catalog.

User operations: Receive an explicit app role; Inspect effective permissions and denial reasons; Access only permitted operations and resource fields.

Delegate access administration or audit for specified applications and business tenants without granting business records or swarm administration. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Core @access-admin and @access-auditor templates have fixed management meanings. Require a current, bound preview before applying role, deny or directory assignment changes. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Management routes enforce same-origin writes, validated input, current actor/revision/source binding and expiring previews. Assign exact experience role templates together with reviewed required and explicitly selected optional application roles. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** CompositeRoleEngine creates child previews through the existing authority and applies members plus provenance in one transaction. ### AUTH-18 — Authorization catalog upgrade review

Keep granted access tied to installed authorization catalog versions and require review when an upgrade widens or breaks access. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Registration snapshots installed provenance and revision. ### AUTH-19 — Personal access tokens for CLI authentication

Allow revocable per-user headless authentication without distributing the swarm service secret. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Tokens are shown once and stored as hashes with owner RLS, expiry and verified issuer. Legacy rows keep an absent issuer rather than inventing one. Bound node and location tokens take separate restricted rails.

User operations: Mint a personal access token; List and revoke owned tokens; Inspect the token-authenticated principal.

The inspected Rust router has sessions and CLI compatibility introspection, not the core per-user PAT mint/list/revoke API with issuer-preserving device/location binding columns. <a id="sec-01"></a>
### SEC-01 — Personal data vault encryption and exact-owner storage

Store a person’s private graph and data in a validated owner-specific vault layout with sensitive-field encryption. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Vault layout maps exact subjects to bound digest directories and rejects linked leaves; vault field crypto binds encryption to the owner. This is distinct from the administrative HashiCorp Vault console.

User operations: Keep personal data under an exact owner; Read supported personal entities and relations; Keep encrypted fields separate from shared data.

Core evidence: [src/features/personal-data/vault.ts](../../src/features/personal-data/vault.ts), [src/features/personal-data/vault-crypto.ts](../../src/features/personal-data/vault-crypto.ts), [src/features/personal-data/sqlite-vault-store.ts](../../src/features/personal-data/sqlite-vault-store.ts), [src/app/routes/personal-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/personal-routes.ts).

Rust: **partial**. SealedVault implements AES-GCM envelope encryption with per-owner DEKs and references; Rust person-model stores and scoped data cover related personal data. This is not a parity proof for core SQLite graph/vault layout or API. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/intents/src/sealed.rs`, `crates/person-model/src/stores.rs`, `crates/control/src/scope_key.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/personal/entities`, `/api/personal/relate`, `/api/personal/contribute`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/057-personal-data-schema.md](../../docs/adr/057-personal-data-schema.md), [docs/adr/058-personal-intelligence-service-and-ingestion.md](../../docs/adr/058-personal-intelligence-service-and-ingestion.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/personal-vault-path-binding.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/personal-vault-path-binding.spec.ts), [tests/unit/data-lifecycle-vault-exact-subject.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/data-lifecycle-vault-exact-subject.spec.ts).

<a id="sec-02"></a>
### SEC-02 — Administrative Vault credential broker

Manage Vault KV secrets and scoped short-lived credential leases through an administrative console. **Core: gated; boundary: shared-engine.** Real HashiCorp Vault HTTP operations are wired behind superadmin checks and confirmation/audit paths. Service comments explicitly scope this built tier to single-admin/single-tenant; multi-user ephemeral runtime isolation remains a separate gated build.

User operations: Inspect Vault health; Read/write/list KV secrets; Issue and revoke scoped leased credentials; Manage policies and database secret roles.

Core evidence: [src/features/devops-vault/services/vault-console-service.ts](../../src/features/devops-vault/services/vault-console-service.ts), [src/app/routes/devops-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/devops-routes.ts), [src/shared/middleware/superadmin.ts](../../src/shared/middleware/superadmin.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust has a sealed secret vault and confirmed master-key rotation endpoint. Inspected vault API does not provide HashiCorp KV/policy/dynamic database lease brokerage or the core console. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/intents/src/sealed.rs`, `crates/api/src/vault_api.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/devops/console`, `/api/devops/status`, `/api/devops/kv/read`, `/api/devops/kv/write`, `/api/devops/issue`, `/api/devops/revoke`, `/api/devops/policy`, `/api/devops/setup-db`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/040-devops-vault-swarm.md](../../docs/adr/040-devops-vault-swarm.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/vault-console-service.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/vault-console-service.spec.ts), [tests/unit/devops-vault-route-gate.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/devops-vault-route-gate.spec.ts).

<a id="sec-03"></a>
### SEC-03 — Owner-qualified connector and AI credential resolution

Resolve credentials for the actual user, issuer and tenant without promoting credential possession into application authority. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Qualified connector brokerage and encryption bind full principal/tenant; callback state is authenticated and one-time. Capability/provider resolution obtains credentials through scoped owner ports, separate from model prompts and application grants.

User operations: Connect a personal provider account; Select an explicitly shared tenant connection when allowed; Use own AI credentials with configured fallback policy.

<a id="sec-04"></a>
### SEC-04 — Interactive tool approvals and protected control events

Pause tools that require human permission and deliver approval controls without releasing pending protected output. **Core: partial; boundary: shared-engine.** Tool policy interceptor, pending request resolver and timeout denial are implemented; protected SSE forwards only canonical approval controls under current pending inline authority. Source-wide search finds resolveApproval only at its declaration: the modal POSTs /api/tools/approval but the inspected tool router has no decision endpoint. Browser approve/deny completion is therefore not established; normal result events remain completion-gated.

User operations: Receive task-bound approval request events; Keep ask-mode tools blocked until a decision; Let unanswered requests time out to denial.

<a id="sec-05"></a>
### SEC-05 — Signed workload delegation and replay containment

Delegate exact cross-process user-data operations through recorded short-lived request-bound authority. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Core issues Ed25519-signed claims only after durable workload scope checks; verifier binds method/path/body/audience/issuer and consumes nonce authority. Legacy service-identity handling has explicit containment modes rather than trusting arbitrary user headers.

User operations: Allow an authorized worker to perform one scoped request; Revoke workload authority; Refuse replayed or mismatched request bindings.

Core evidence: [src/shared/security/delegation-token.ts](../../src/shared/security/delegation-token.ts), [src/shared/security/delegation-request-binding.ts](../../src/shared/security/delegation-request-binding.ts), [src/shared/security/delegation-replay-store.ts](../../src/shared/security/delegation-replay-store.ts), [src/features/security/workload-delegation-issuer.ts](../../src/features/security/workload-delegation-issuer.ts), [src/features/security/workload-delegation-middleware.ts](../../src/features/security/workload-delegation-middleware.ts), [src/features/security/legacy-service-identity-containment.ts](../../src/features/security/legacy-service-identity-containment.ts).

Bounded api/oshald search found no integration of Delegations redemption into HTTP admission or durable workload authority; this is an implemented primitive, not the wired core cross-process protocol. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/control/src/delegation.rs`, `crates/api/src/extract.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/signin.rs`.

<a id="sec-06"></a>
### SEC-06 — Durable protected remote and inline result authority

Preserve original grants, package provenance and exact owner through execution and reauthorize before history or output release. **Core: partial; boundary: shared-engine.** Remote permit lifecycle and controller-only startInline/completeInline share durable authority, current owner/policy/snapshot checks and original ceilings. Empty admission requires zero actual messages and current ownership; nonempty no-lineage history remains refused. Inline records are controller provenance, not forged signed worker permits. Current registrations mint a random generation at each API boot, and assertSnapshot requires exact generation equality; prior protected answers are therefore fenced after restart. Stable release identity for durable history remains incomplete.

User operations: Open an owned empty protected conversation; Receive only completed currently authorized results; Recover a conversation without bypassing changed grants.

Core evidence: [src/features/application-remote-execution/service.ts](../../src/features/application-remote-execution/service.ts), [src/features/application-remote-execution/store.ts](../../src/features/application-remote-execution/store.ts), [src/app/routes/protected-inline-execution.ts](../../src/app/routes/protected-inline-execution.ts), [src/app/routes/protected-empty-task-access.ts](../../src/app/routes/protected-empty-task-access.ts), [src/app/routes/protected-result-access.ts](../../src/app/routes/protected-result-access.ts), [src/shared/protected-results/index.ts](../../src/shared/protected-results/index.ts), [src/app/composition/application-authorization-runtime.ts](../../src/app/composition/application-authorization-runtime.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust dispatch envelopes, node generation/lease checks and owner-scoped task stores provide execution accountability. Bounded control/nodes/orchestration/api search did not locate a durable completed application-result authority equivalent carrying original named grants plus catalog/source snapshot into inline history/SSE release. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/orchestration/src/dispatch.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/enrollment.rs`, `crates/control/src/ctx.rs`, `crates/api/src/tickets.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/tasks/:taskId`, `/api/:taskId/messages`, `/api/stream/:taskId`.

Carry verified request identity into database operations and enforce ownership/tenant access beneath routes. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** AsyncLocalStorage carries subject, issuer and operator/system distinction; GUC pool stamps per-client context and strict-mode absence denies. Core includes owner/tenant RLS and least-privilege roles; individual legacy schemas still differ in issuer coverage.

<a id="exec-17"></a>
### EXEC-17 — Bot-owned RCA methods with deterministic result validation

RcaEngine supports five-whys, fishbone and fault-tree prompts, invokes an injected analysis executor and validates the resulting root causes, recommendations and bounded confidence. **Core: gated; boundary: shared-engine.** The authenticated /api/rca/analyze route constructs RcaEngine over executeBotOrInline targeting rca-specialist with caller subject and task accountability. Reasoning is performed by the bot/model; JSON extraction, required-field validation and confidence clamping are deterministic. No configured executor, disabled mode or unusable response causes an explicit failure rather than placeholder causes. Route maps disabled to 501, backend failure to 503 and identified budget/entitlement failures to 429/403. Execution depends on bot/provider and authorization availability; this is not a deterministic root-cause inference algorithm.

User operations: Request a selected RCA method for an incident; Receive a structured validated verdict; See explicit disabled, unavailable, budget or entitlement responses.

Core evidence: [src/features/rca-analysis/index.ts](../../src/features/rca-analysis/index.ts), [src/features/rca-analysis/services/rca-engine.ts](../../src/features/rca-analysis/services/rca-engine.ts), [src/app/routes/rca-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/rca-routes.ts), [src/app/routes/inline-bot-execution.ts](../../src/app/routes/inline-bot-execution.ts), [src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts](../../src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts).

Rust: **not-located**. Rust has generic bot turn execution and health/remediation primitives. A corresponding five-whys/fishbone/fault-tree RCA engine, structured verdict validation and existing /api/rca/analyze payload/error contract were not located in reviewed Rust orchestration/health/API code. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/orchestration/src/turn.rs`, `crates/health/src/remediation.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/rca/analyze`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/036-bot-owned-application-architecture.md](../../docs/adr/036-bot-owned-application-architecture.md), [docs/adr/119-autonomous-health-ticket-processing.md](../../docs/adr/119-autonomous-health-ticket-processing.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/rca-engine.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/rca-engine.spec.ts).

<a id="model-01"></a>
### MODEL-01 — Unified provider request and response port

LLMService normalizes messages, tool schemas, streaming callbacks, usage and model attribution across providers. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** The named contract is LLMService with SendRequestOptions/LLMResponse; do not infer extra numbered layers from product terminology.

User operations: Use a provider through a common API; Receive streaming responses and normalized token usage.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/llm-service.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/llm-service.ts), [src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts](../../src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts).

Rust: **wired**. Rust Provider/CompletionRequest/Completion and scoped inference are wired for OpenAI, Anthropic and noop; wire compatibility with LLMService is not claimed. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/inference/src/provider.rs`, `crates/inference/src/scoped.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/020-openai-codex-runtime-provider-wiring.md](../../docs/adr/020-openai-codex-runtime-provider-wiring.md).

<a id="model-02"></a>
### MODEL-02 — Hosted model provider adapters

Direct Anthropic and per-user hosted/OpenAI-compatible providers perform network model calls behind the provider port. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Direct adapters exist; availability still requires usable credentials and current provider admission.

User operations: Run a hosted model; Choose a model and endpoint supported by the configured adapter.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/anthropic-provider.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/anthropic-provider.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/byo-hosted-provider.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/byo-hosted-provider.ts), [src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts](../../src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts).

Rust: **wired**. Rust real OpenAI/Anthropic adapters are registered in Installation; endpoint/secret resolver configuration is supported. Other original vendor-specific adapter parity is not assumed. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/inference/src/openai.rs`, `crates/inference/src/anthropic.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/173-capability-providers-resolve-per-user.md](../../docs/adr/173-capability-providers-resolve-per-user.md).

<a id="model-03"></a>
### MODEL-03 — Provider and model catalog with capability metadata

ProviderRegistry supplies selectable provider/model definitions, token limits, price metadata and capability flags. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Catalog entries are selectable definitions, not a claim that each provider is authenticated or runnable.

User operations: Discover supported providers and models; Select a suitable model by its advertised capabilities.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-registry.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-registry.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-definitions.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-definitions.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-catalog.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-catalog.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust registers provider implementations and prices but the existing multi-vendor catalog, capability metadata and selectable local-service definitions were not located. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/inference/src/provider.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md](../../docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/config-admin-capability-providers.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/config-admin-capability-providers.spec.ts).

<a id="model-05"></a>
### MODEL-05 — Layered bot brain records and hot provider switching

Per-bot and fleet switch records resolve before agent-config and registry defaults; dispatch carries the chosen record and configured fallback order. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** ProviderSwitchStore and dispatch-runtime-params are the current runtime record seams, distinct from a user preference.

User operations: Change a bot or fleet provider without editing every caller; Keep the chosen configuration bound to a dispatch.

Core route references: `/api/agents/provider-switch`, `/api/agents/provider-switch/fleet-default`.

<a id="model-06"></a>
### MODEL-06 — Retry classification and configured provider failover

Transient provider failures can retry the same endpoint or follow the explicitly configured failover chain without replaying a whole tool turn. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** SameEndpointRetry and ProviderFailoverService are separate runtime mechanisms; fallback does not mean arbitrary account switching.

User operations: Survive a transient model outage; Receive a truthful cause when no admissible fallback is available.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/same-endpoint-retry.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/same-endpoint-retry.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-failover-service.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/provider-failover-service.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/hot-fallback-chain-provider.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/hot-fallback-chain-provider.ts), [src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts](../../src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust provider errors and mesh retries exist; original same-call retry classifier and operator-written provider failover chain equivalence was not located. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/inference/src/provider.rs`, `crates/mesh/src/queue.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/162-a-bots-brain-is-layered-records.md](../../docs/adr/162-a-bots-brain-is-layered-records.md).

GovernedProvider wraps model calls with budget, quota and fallback-routing decisions. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** GovernedProvider is imported by the provider composition root; policy configuration determines enforcement.

<a id="model-08"></a>

Persisted persona layers compose a bot prompt while prompt containment and task framing keep model input separate from authority. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** PersonaLayerType names platform, host, tenant, role, session and task; the composer sorts by priority. These are prompt-composition types, separate from provider/tool/harness terminology.

User operations: Customize bot behavior through persona layers; Preserve the chosen bot role and task frame.

<a id="harness-01"></a>
### HARNESS-01 — Typed harness adapter and factory selection

HarnessAdapter runs a HarnessTask and returns a normalized HarnessResult; typed factory/default maps choose the declared runtime. **Core: wired; boundary: node.** HarnessType names Cline, Codex CLI, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, A2A and noop; selectable does not guarantee current host readiness.

User operations: Choose a harness independently from its backing model; Receive normalized work output and usage.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/harness-adapter.ts), [src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts](../../src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust models harnesses as enrolled nodes rather than kernel-spawned adapters. Node protocol exists, but current original harness factories/adapters are not supplied by Rust inference. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/inference/src/lib.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/lib.rs`, `crates/api/src/nodes_api.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md](../../docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md).

<a id="harness-02"></a>
### HARNESS-02 — Local CLI agent runtime adapters

Concrete CLI adapters build vendor arguments, execute the runtime and parse output/usage into the shared harness port. **Core: gated; boundary: node.** Cline, Codex, Claude, Gemini and Antigravity code exists; binaries, credentials, unattended policy and node-runtime readiness are explicit prerequisites.

User operations: Run coding or reasoning through an installed CLI agent; Use its authenticated local account where allowed.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/cline-cli-wrapper.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/cline-cli-wrapper.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/codex-cli-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/codex-cli-harness-adapter.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/claude-code-cli-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/claude-code-cli-harness-adapter.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/gemini-cli-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/gemini-cli-harness-adapter.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/antigravity-cli-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/antigravity-cli-harness-adapter.ts).

Rust: **not-located**. No equivalent shipped vendor CLI harness adapters were located in the reviewed Rust daemon/node sources; its node enrollment contract alone is not an installed harness. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/nodes/src/lib.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/main.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md](../../docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/harness-idle-timeouts.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/harness-idle-timeouts.spec.ts), [tests/unit/antigravity-host-tool-loop.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/antigravity-host-tool-loop.spec.ts).

<a id="harness-03"></a>
### HARNESS-03 — External A2A agent delegation

A2AHarnessAdapter delegates work to a configured external agent and records remote usage under the appropriate task/bot. **Core: gated; boundary: node.** Endpoint, credential and outbound capability policy are required; A2A is a typed registered harness.

User operations: Dispatch to an external agent service; Retain remote outcome and cost attribution.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/a2a-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/a2a-harness-adapter.ts), [src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts](../../src/app/composition/provider-runtime.ts), [src/app/composition/a2a-cost-stamper.ts](../../src/app/composition/a2a-cost-stamper.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust external-agent gateway primitives and remote-node delivery exist; compatibility with the original A2A JSON-RPC harness and cost stamper was not established. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/mesh/src/transports.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md](../../docs/adr/033-multi-harness-execution-framework.md).

<a id="harness-04"></a>
### HARNESS-04 — Harness timeouts, login readiness and unattended policy

Base CLI runtime handling imposes idle/wall deadlines and checks whether unattended execution and credentials are actually available. **Core: gated; boundary: node.** BaseCliHarnessAdapter and user-brain offer checks are implemented; vendor availability is not treated as a successful execution.

User operations: Avoid indefinitely hanging subprocess work; Receive a readiness refusal before an unavailable CLI is offered.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/base-cli-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/base-cli-harness-adapter.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/unattended-provider-policy.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/unattended-provider-policy.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/gemini-auth-status-service.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/gemini-auth-status-service.ts), [src/app/routes/user-brain-resolution.ts](../../src/app/routes/user-brain-resolution.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust node leases and scoped admission constrain remote work, but original CLI idle-timeout/login adoption/readiness checks were not located. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/nodes/src/lease.rs`, `crates/control/src/kernel.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/127-demo-mode-cli-brain-and-user-provider-preference.md](../../docs/adr/127-demo-mode-cli-brain-and-user-provider-preference.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/harness-idle-timeouts.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/harness-idle-timeouts.spec.ts), [tests/unit/cli-brain-executability.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/cli-brain-executability.spec.ts).

<a id="harness-05"></a>
### HARNESS-05 — Bot runtime launcher abstraction and managed configuration

Docker/compose and Kubernetes launchers, runtime manifests and provider snapshots configure a bot runtime under declared identity. **Core: wired; boundary: node.** Launcher resolver, Kubernetes launcher and runtime-manifest/config sync implementations exist; deploy platform/config determines active launcher.

User operations: Start a bot runtime on the selected platform; Push the chosen provider configuration to a worker.

Core evidence: [src/features/agent-management/services/bot-runtime-launcher.ts](../../src/features/agent-management/services/bot-runtime-launcher.ts), [src/features/agent-management/services/bot-runtime-launcher-resolver.ts](../../src/features/agent-management/services/bot-runtime-launcher-resolver.ts), [src/features/agent-management/services/kubernetes-bot-launcher.ts](../../src/features/agent-management/services/kubernetes-bot-launcher.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/agent-startup-manifest-service.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/agent-startup-manifest-service.ts), [src/features/agent-management/services/provider-switch-snapshot.ts](../../src/features/agent-management/services/provider-switch-snapshot.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust node enrollment and daemon packaging exist; equivalent Docker/Kubernetes bot-runtime provisioning and original startup manifest/config sync were not located. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/nodes/src/enrollment.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/config.rs`.

<a id="tool-02"></a>
### TOOL-02 — Auto, ask and off tool switches with auth groups

Per-agent tool switches track installation/configuration and change automatic, approval-required or disabled authorization, including grouped changes. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** SwitchFrameworkService and AgentToolController are mounted at /api/agents. <a id="tool-09"></a>
### TOOL-09 — RAG ingestion integration and caller-scoped query tools

RAGIngestionIntegrationService exposes health/status and ingestion to a configured service; ToolExecutorService supports external ingestion or built-in RagService ingestion plus permission-scoped retrieval. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** ToolExecutorService dispatches rag-ingestion and rag-query. Configured external endpoints use the integration POST /ingest and GET /health client; without that endpoint it calls built-in RagService. Generic collection restrictions are checked before ingest. Query supplies userSub and allowPublic when acting for a user, and system dispatch retains the unfiltered branch. ToolVerificationService additionally uses the integration healthcheck. The external /health and /ingest URLs are client-side service contracts, not asserted mounted core endpoints; no provider/network execution was performed.

User operations: Ingest knowledge through an agent tool; Query personal and shared accessible knowledge; Check an external ingestion service before use.

Core evidence: [src/features/tool-integrations/index.ts](../../src/features/tool-integrations/index.ts), [src/features/tool-integrations/rag-ingestion-integration.ts](../../src/features/tool-integrations/rag-ingestion-integration.ts), [src/features/chat-orchestration/services/tool-executor-service.ts](../../src/features/chat-orchestration/services/tool-executor-service.ts), [src/features/tool-verification/services/tool-verification-service.ts](../../src/features/tool-verification/services/tool-verification-service.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust has scoped knowledge HTTP ingestion/retrieval, collection/index primitives and Chroma/WADB clients. Compatibility with the external RAG integration health/status protocol, existing rag-ingestion/rag-query tool names and arguments, generic collection restrictions and caller ACL behavior was not established. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/api/src/knowledge_api.rs`, `crates/knowledge/src/lib.rs`, `crates/knowledge/src/vector_store.rs`, `crates/orchestration/src/turn.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/091-pgvector-rag-engine.md](../../docs/adr/091-pgvector-rag-engine.md), [docs/adr/010-layer1-tools-framework.md](../../docs/adr/010-layer1-tools-framework.md).

GoogleSearchIntegration calls configured Google Custom Search and counts usage; KnowledgeEnhancementService limits an explicit query batch, formats source results and ingests them into a knowledge collection while recording per-query failures. **Core: implemented; boundary: shared-engine.** Concrete search and enhancement classes and tests exist. <a id="tool-11"></a>
### TOOL-11 — Agent personal-finance ledger import, analysis and report tools

PersonalFinanceIntegrationService stores a per-agent JSON ledger, normalizes/imports file or inline transactions with ID deduplication, computes spending/budget summaries and generates Markdown reports. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** ToolExecutorService dispatches finance-import, finance-report, analyze-spending and check-budget; it resolves task file paths and builds the integration with an agent-specific runtime directory and agent budget/lookback configuration. The integration performs persisted ledger import, deterministic spending/recurrence/threshold summaries and report generation. This is a tool library implementation rather than the finance application HTTP API, and should not be conflated with vendor account linking or synchronization.

User operations: Import and deduplicate transactions for a configured finance bot; Analyze categories, merchants, months and budget variance; Write a finance report into the task workspace.

Rust: **not-located**. Generic Rust tool execution exists. Equivalent per-agent ledger import/normalization/deduplication, deterministic budget/spending calculation and Markdown report adapter were not located in reviewed Rust source. A static finance package page or example summary response would not establish this tool implementation. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/orchestration/src/turn.rs`, `crates/intents/src/registry.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`.

<a id="tool-12"></a>
### TOOL-12 — Workflow Studio agent-tool HTTP translation contract

WorkflowStudioIntegrationService translates workflow-studio tool actions into local Workflow Studio catalog, definition, validation, compile, duplication and immutable-version API requests. **Core: partial; boundary: package-boundary.** ToolExecutorService constructs the integration for the local /api/workflow-studio base URL and dispatches the workflow-studio tool. The integration implements get/post/put and all named actions, while target routes are mounted with requiresAuth. Reviewed fetch calls carry no forwarded caller authorization/session headers, so successful authorization across this agent-tool-to-local-API boundary is not established from the implementation; mark partial rather than count the HTTP client as a working authenticated workflow author. Existing mounted server routes belong to the Workflow Studio capability; this integration itself mounts no new route.

User operations: Let a configured agent draft or inspect a workflow definition; Validate or compile a definition from a tool action; Read or fork definition versions.

<a id="a2a-01"></a>
### A2A-01 — External agent discovery card

Publish a standards-shaped discovery card for external agents only when the gateway is enabled. **Core: gated; boundary: platform.** Well-known card and RPC surface return unavailable until A2A_GATEWAY_ENABLED. Skill card comes from registered platform capabilities; route is intentionally public discovery, separate from per-agent RPC authentication.

User operations: Discover supported external agent skills; Read gateway identity and transport information.

Core evidence: [src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-agent-card-service.ts](../../src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-agent-card-service.ts), [src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-gateway-config.ts](../../src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-gateway-config.ts), [src/app/routes/a2a-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/a2a-routes.ts).

Rust: **implemented**. Rust Gateway implements enabled/disabled AgentCard and daemon holds a gateway instance. Bounded api router/content search found no well-known card HTTP route; engine existence is not external wire compatibility. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/agents/src/gateway.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`.

Core route references: `/.well-known/agent-card.json`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md](../../docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/a2a-gateway.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/a2a-gateway.spec.ts), [tests/unit/a2a-local-enable-wiring.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/a2a-local-enable-wiring.spec.ts).

<a id="a2a-02"></a>
### A2A-02 — Inbound A2A ticket protocol

Translate authenticated external-agent message and task requests onto real ticket execution rails. **Core: gated; boundary: shared-engine.** JSON-RPC supports message/send, tasks/get and tasks/cancel, attributes tickets to the per-agent synthetic owner, checks scopes and applies fail-closed inbound ceilings. It dispatches through ticket/queue rails rather than selecting a model in the gateway.

User operations: Submit an A2A message as a real ticket; Read the submitting agent’s task status/artifacts; Cancel a cancelable task.

Core evidence: [src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-rpc-service.ts](../../src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-rpc-service.ts), [src/app/routes/a2a-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/a2a-routes.ts), [src/shared/types/a2a.ts](../../src/shared/types/a2a.ts).

Rust: **not-located**. Bounded agents/api/oshald source search for JSON-RPC, agent-card, message/send and tasks/get/cancel found no corresponding HTTP protocol handlers. Generic gateway and outbound transport traits are narrower engine primitives. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/agents/src/gateway.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/a2a`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md](../../docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/a2a-gateway.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/a2a-gateway.spec.ts).

<a id="a2a-03"></a>
### A2A-03 — Per-external-agent credentials and revocation

Enroll each external agent with its own revocable credential and declared scopes. **Core: gated; boundary: platform.** Management routes require authenticated operator access; RPC uses the agent’s own bearer identity and scopes, not a browser session or a fleet service secret.

User operations: Register an external agent credential; List enrolled agents; Revoke one agent without affecting others.

Core evidence: [src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-credentials-service.ts](../../src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-credentials-service.ts), [src/app/routes/a2a-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/a2a-routes.ts), [src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-gateway-config.ts](../../src/features/a2a-gateway/services/a2a-gateway-config.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust Gateway enrol/admit/revoke implements independent digest credentials, scopes and confirmed-access opt-in. The inspected HTTP router lacks the core external-agent management endpoints and bearer gateway integration. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/agents/src/gateway.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/a2a/agents`, `/api/a2a/agents/:id/revoke`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md](../../docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/a2a-gateway.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/a2a-gateway.spec.ts).

<a id="a2a-04"></a>
### A2A-04 — Outbound external-agent harness and cost attribution

Call a registered external agent through the harness abstraction and attribute reported costs to the actual originating work. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** A2A harness adapter normalizes the external protocol; cost events and controller stamper associate execution/task ownership rather than accepting caller-invented attribution. Availability depends on configured endpoint and credentials.

User operations: Choose a registered A2A harness; Receive normalized external-agent output; Track externally reported task costs separately from metered provider usage.

Core evidence: [src/features/llm-provider/services/a2a-harness-adapter.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/a2a-harness-adapter.ts), [src/features/llm-provider/services/a2a-cost-events.ts](../../src/features/llm-provider/services/a2a-cost-events.ts), [src/app/composition/a2a-cost-stamper.ts](../../src/app/composition/a2a-cost-stamper.ts).

Rust: **implemented**. Rust Outbound checks current gateway identity and ceiling, scrubs input/output and records reported cost through AgentTransport. A concrete A2A network adapter or core harness registration was not located in bounded agents/api/oshald search. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/agents/src/outbound.rs`, `crates/agents/src/gateway.rs`, `crates/control/src/ctx.rs`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md](../../docs/adr/109-a2a-gateway-external-agents-join-the-swarm.md), [docs/adr/104-cost-governance-budgets-and-runaway-kill-switch.md](../../docs/adr/104-cost-governance-budgets-and-runaway-kill-switch.md).

<a id="node-01"></a>
### NODE-01 — Owner-bound node enrollment

Enroll a remote machine with a device identity tied to its verified enrolling user. **Core: wired; boundary: node.** Join enrollment defaults to a server-generated bound clientId and token owner issuer; registration checks the declared body ID against token binding. Legacy operator join codes remain a distinct compatibility rail.

User operations: Enroll a desktop node; Receive a device-specific credential once; Verify node ownership before registration.

Rust: **wired**. Confirmed owner-scoped join-code creation, single-use redemption, device-token digests and enrollment owner/tenant state are wired to actual nodes HTTP routes and the native node client. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/api/src/nodes_api.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/joining.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/enrollment.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/token.rs`, `crates/oshal-node/src/client.rs`.

<a id="node-02"></a>
### NODE-02 — Device credential confinement and package node rails

Confine device credentials to their own worker plane and declared owning-application node endpoints. **Core: wired; boundary: package-boundary.** Node-bound PATs cannot use ordinary account APIs. Current source additionally restricts package rails to /api/<app>/<segment>, binds app rails to clientId app prefix and removes rails before remount. These recent source edits were observed during an active builder lane; publication/deployment parity was not checked.

User operations: Rotate a node token; Revoke a lost node credential; Use device APIs without granting full account access.

Core evidence: [src/features/remote-client/services/node-token-scope.ts](../../src/features/remote-client/services/node-token-scope.ts), [src/app/routes/cli-token-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/cli-token-routes.ts), [src/app/routes/remote-client-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/remote-client-routes.ts), [src/app/composition/manifest-route-mounter.ts](../../src/app/composition/manifest-route-mounter.ts).

Rust: **partial**. Rust device tokens bind enrolled node/owner and validate lease/generation on node routes. No core manifest auth:node rail registry or application-clientId namespace protocol was located in inspected api/nodes/package route source. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/nodes/src/token.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/enrollment.rs`, `crates/api/src/nodes_api.rs`, `crates/api/src/packages_api.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/remote-clients/:clientId/token/rotate`, `/api/remote-clients/:clientId/heartbeat`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/175-package-device-nodes-use-device-bound-credentials.md](../../docs/adr/175-package-device-nodes-use-device-bound-credentials.md), [docs/adr/114-user-owned-remote-nodes.md](../../docs/adr/114-user-owned-remote-nodes.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/remote-client-node-token.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/remote-client-node-token.spec.ts), [tests/unit/package-node-rail.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/package-node-rail.spec.ts).

<a id="node-03"></a>
### NODE-03 — Remote node registry, liveness and ownership

Track enrolled clients and expose only devices a caller or authorized dispatcher may use. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Remote registry tracks clients and heartbeat; owner/operator policy gates HTTP and internal selection, denying unknown owners unless a named legacy switch is enabled. Device policy includes explicit trusted-system paths rather than silently treating absent user identity as ownership.

User operations: List reachable owned nodes; Inspect heartbeat and capability status; Keep re-registration attached to the same owner; Choose an authorized node for work.

Core evidence: [src/features/remote-client/services/remote-client-registry.ts](../../src/features/remote-client/services/remote-client-registry.ts), [src/features/remote-client/services/device-access.ts](../../src/features/remote-client/services/device-access.ts), [src/features/remote-client/services/remote-client-rate-limit.ts](../../src/features/remote-client/services/remote-client-rate-limit.ts), [src/app/routes/remote-client-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/remote-client-routes.ts).

Rust: **wired**. Enrollment visible_to scopes node listing to owner; heartbeat verifies device token and generation, renews lease, and native NodeAgent ticks that rail. Protocol and registry shape differ from core remote-client routes. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/nodes/src/enrollment.rs`, `crates/nodes/src/lease.rs`, `crates/api/src/nodes_api.rs`, `crates/oshal-node/src/agent.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/remote-clients`, `/api/remote-clients/:clientId`, `/api/remote-clients/:clientId/heartbeat`, `/api/remote-clients/:clientId/owner`.

<a id="node-04"></a>
### NODE-04 — Remote task claim, completion and durable results

Dispatch scoped work to remote clients and settle results through identity-bound task journals. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** HTTP device checks, task identity, durable journal, completion callbacks and result projections preserve originating work and owner. Protected bot-node execution additionally requires controller permits and original application grant evidence.

<a id="node-08"></a>
### NODE-08 — Bot-node pools and scarce resource leases

Allocate worker nodes and coordinate exclusive use of scarce physical rendering or execution resources. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Pool routes are worker-secret gated; allocator validates endpoints. PostgreSQL resource leases use exact capability ID and expiry so a stale holder cannot release a successor; protected workers use separate signed/controller authority.

User operations: Assign and release a pool worker; Inspect worker status; Acquire, renew or release an exact resource lease.

Core route references: `/node/assign`, `/node/release`, `/node/status`.

<a id="mon-10"></a>
### MON-10 — Operations Stream event, decision, incident and action evidence

Alertmanager and native internal events land durably, claim a decision, consolidate an incident/ticket, and record per-event side effects and dispatch evidence; health/funnel/trend and operator routing/replay/topology surfaces expose the pipeline. **Core: wired; boundary: shared-engine.** Alertmanager is mounted under /api/alerts; durable PostgreSQL mode acknowledges 202 only after envelope/event landing and uses locked pending-event claims. Event effects record intake, consolidation, member and dispatch effects to contain replay duplication. Ops router mounts only with a pool; reads require auth and rule/topology/replay routes additionally require operator on each route. A0/A1/A2 autonomy remains bounded by the alert-triage execution policy. Topology and incident stores are implemented; this does not assert every estate discovery driver or every ADR rollout gap is complete.

User operations: Trace a received alert through admission and action; Consolidate repeat events into an accountable incident; Inspect pipeline health and missing intake; Review claim rules, topology and bounded event replay.

<a id="mon-11"></a>
### MON-11 — Argo one-shot phase execution and durable batch-job telemetry

A bot-node batch entrypoint runs one phase using the shared node execution handler, writes the RCA MODE output for an Argo DAG, exits by result and persists worker/queue, runtime, CPU/memory, provider/model/cost and failure observations. **Core: gated; boundary: node.** bot-node-batch invokes createBotNodeRuntime and executionHandler under system identity, writes mode.txt and records non-fatal telemetry in oshal_batch_job_runs. /api/batch-jobs/recent and /report are authenticated; recent reads scope to caller unless authorized operator scope is selected. PostgreSQL is required for stored runs. Critical current gate: assertDelegationBatchRuntimeAllowed prohibits batch startup whenever delegation verification is configured because this runtime lacks a signed HTTP request/replay ledger. Thus code exists but enterprise delegation rollout can disable Argo execution. Historical capture and CPU-over-time gaps are explicitly returned by the route; no live Argo deployment or run was assessed.

User operations: Run an eligible workflow phase as a one-shot batch worker; Branch an incident DAG using the phase MODE; Review caller-scoped recent batch runs and runtime/resource reports.

Core evidence: [src/features/batch-job-telemetry/index.ts](../../src/features/batch-job-telemetry/index.ts), [src/features/batch-job-telemetry/services/batch-job-telemetry-store.ts](../../src/features/batch-job-telemetry/services/batch-job-telemetry-store.ts), [src/app/bot-node-batch.ts](../../src/app/bot-node-batch.ts), [src/app/bot-node-batch-telemetry.ts](../../src/app/bot-node-batch-telemetry.ts), [src/app/bot-node-delegation.ts](../../src/app/bot-node-delegation.ts), [src/app/routes/batch-job-telemetry-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/batch-job-telemetry-routes.ts), [src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts](../../src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts).

Rust: **not-located**. Rust node daemon/configuration and ordinary workflow/turn execution exist; an equivalent Argo one-shot phase worker, MODE output, oshal_batch_job_runs telemetry persistence and caller-scoped batch report contract were not located in reviewed node/orchestration/API source. Kubernetes deployment by itself does not establish this job execution/capture feature. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/oshal-node/src/main.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/config.rs`, `crates/orchestration/src/turn.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`.

Core route references: `/api/batch-jobs/recent`, `/api/batch-jobs/report`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/078-kubernetes-argo-batch-and-multi-tenant-proofout.md](../../docs/adr/078-kubernetes-argo-batch-and-multi-tenant-proofout.md), [docs/adr/149-enterprise-application-authorization.md](../../docs/adr/149-enterprise-application-authorization.md).

<a id="learn-04"></a>
### LEARN-04 — Post-exchange passive learner

After successful Jarvis exchanges, throttled extraction runs on the supplied accountable Jarvis brain, merges safe facts and stores evidence in the owner-scoped long-tail corpus. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Jarvis-orchestrator calls learnFromExchange after answers on both inspected entry paths. Default learning enabled; OSHAL_USER_MODEL_LEARN disables it; short turns and per-user throttle suppress unnecessary extraction.

User operations: Let ordinary assistant conversations improve remembered preferences and facts; Use accumulated learning on later exchanges.

Core evidence: [src/features/user-model/services/haven-context-service.ts](../../src/features/user-model/services/haven-context-service.ts), [src/features/user-model/services/user-model-service.ts](../../src/features/user-model/services/user-model-service.ts), [src/features/user-model/services/user-model-logic.ts](../../src/features/user-model/services/user-model-logic.ts), [src/app/routes/jarvis-orchestrator.ts](../../src/app/routes/jarvis-orchestrator.ts).

<a id="ambient-03"></a>
### AMBIENT-03 — Ambient retention and confirmed privacy erasure

Applies owner retention to transcripts/reviews and receipt cleanup, supports deleting a selected day, and confirms full transcript/review/receipt and remembered-speaker cleanup while disabling capture. **Core: wired; boundary: platform.** Forced owner RLS and owner predicates protect the durable store. <a id="social-01"></a>
### SOCIAL-01 — Retained LinkedIn draft assistant and queue integration

Generates owner-scoped LinkedIn drafts on social-writer, grades against the LinkedIn rubric, makes at most one interactive refine pass and retains the better graded result; approval/rejection follow a persisted legal state machine. Bound queue work stores draft, citations and source-ticket provenance. **Core: wired; boundary: resident-application.** The retained /api/linkedin-assistant router is auth-mounted in core even though the broader Social app moved to applications; server comments reference ADR-093 for placement. The composition root supplies the LinkedIn queue binding. Real generation requires an available authorized social-writer/provider; queue use requires its registered manifest workflow. Judge mode records model versus lexical fallback. Approval stamps a scheduled time; automatic timed publication is not claimed.

User operations: Generate, inspect and judge a LinkedIn draft before publication; Approve into a posting slot or reject the draft; Produce a draft from an authorized queue ticket and retain its citations.

Core evidence: [src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/linkedin-content-service.ts](../../src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/linkedin-content-service.ts), [src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/content-draft-store.ts](../../src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/content-draft-store.ts), [src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/draft-state-machine.ts](../../src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/draft-state-machine.ts), [src/features/linkedin-assistant/types/draft.ts](../../src/features/linkedin-assistant/types/draft.ts), [src/app/routes/linkedin-assistant-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/linkedin-assistant-routes.ts), [src/app/linkedin-content-queue-workflow.ts](../../src/app/linkedin-content-queue-workflow.ts), [src/app/linkedin-content-ticket-provenance.ts](../../src/app/linkedin-content-ticket-provenance.ts), [src/app/composition-root.ts](../../src/app/composition-root.ts), [src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts](../../src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts), [src/app/server.ts](../../src/app/server.ts).

Rust: **not-located**. No corresponding retained LinkedIn draft store, state lifecycle, judged/refined drafting or queue-to-draft binding was located in reviewed Rust runtime code. Generic connectors and quality types alone do not establish this domain workflow. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/api/src/router.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`, `crates/optimize/src/lib.rs`.

<a id="social-02"></a>
### SOCIAL-02 — Approved LinkedIn publication with connector and ticket provenance

Publishes the exact approved scheduled draft through the declarative LinkedIn create-post executor, with explicit human confirmation, lazy caller-scoped broker credentials, compare-and-swap publish claim, connector audit hash and source-ticket outcome writeback. **Core: wired; boundary: resident-application.** Publication additionally requires explicit route confirmation, a scheduled approved draft, the loadable LinkedIn connector and a usable personal/shared connection with author id. Missing connection returns a clean skip and leaves the draft scheduled; concurrent publish claims prevent duplicate live POSTs, and failed attempts release the claim. This is a resident application workflow rather than a universal kernel primitive.

User operations: Publish an approved draft to the connected LinkedIn account; See connection refusals without a fabricated successful post; Trace the published post and audit hash back to its draft and originating ticket.

Core evidence: [src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/linkedin-content-service.ts](../../src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/linkedin-content-service.ts), [src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/content-draft-store.ts](../../src/features/linkedin-assistant/services/content-draft-store.ts), [src/app/routes/linkedin-assistant-routes.ts](../../src/app/routes/linkedin-assistant-routes.ts), [src/app/linkedin-content-ticket-provenance.ts](../../src/app/linkedin-content-ticket-provenance.ts), [src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts](../../src/app/server-auxiliary-routes.ts), [swarm-apps/connectors/linkedin.yaml](../../swarm-apps/connectors/linkedin.yaml).

Rust: **not-located**. Rust configuration declares LinkedIn OAuth endpoints, but equivalent confirmed approved-draft publication, domain state fencing, audited post/draft/ticket provenance and failure-release handling were not located in reviewed runtime sources. Sources in `oshal-kernel`: `crates/oshald/src/config.rs`, `crates/api/src/router.rs`, `crates/oshald/src/lib.rs`.

Core route references: `POST /api/linkedin-assistant/drafts/:id/publish`.

Decisions: [docs/adr/036-bot-owned-application-architecture.md](../../docs/adr/036-bot-owned-application-architecture.md), [docs/adr/093-packaged-app-runtime-placement.md](../../docs/adr/093-packaged-app-runtime-placement.md).

Existing acceptance sources: [tests/unit/linkedin-assistant.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/linkedin-assistant.spec.ts), [tests/unit/connectors/connector-write-actions.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/connectors/connector-write-actions.spec.ts), [tests/unit/linkedin-content-queue-postgres.spec.ts](../../tests/unit/linkedin-content-queue-postgres.spec.ts).

## Current ADR coverage

All numbered ADR files are listed by exact filename, preserving duplicate numbers and suffix variants. Assignments mean a feature cites that decision; they are not a claim that all of its requirements are met. The initial unassigned set received a separate bounded review: classifications distinguish already-covered core, package domains, proposals, governance, superseded history and numerical reference implementations. Related records indicate capability coverage without pretending that a missing citation is an implementation omission.

The September clean-kernel import map is a dated draft. Its proposed “superseded” labels do not retire current features, and its maximum ADR number does not bound this inventory.

## Maintenance and acceptance

Edit [core-feature-inventory.json](./core-feature-inventory.json), then regenerate. Keep each user capability tied to concrete implementation/caller sources and mark configuration or rollout gates. When changing a source baseline, reassess its claims; changing a revision string alone is not verification.

```sh
node scripts/core-feature-inventory.js
node scripts/core-feature-inventory.js --check
node scripts/core-feature-inventory.js --check --rust-root ../../oshal-kernel
node scripts/docs-link-check.js
```

The generator validates core source, ADR and test file references, row IDs/states, current skill declarations and source/ADR coverage, and checks generated Markdown determinism. The optional Rust root validates the cited Rust paths without requiring a sibling repository in CI. It executes no application, provider request, migration or database mutation.

A full replacement verdict still requires authorized browser journeys, real execution, dependency/composite-role provisioning, result/accounting lineage and preserved ownership/data semantics on an identified deployed build. Use the existing test references as a starting acceptance matrix; this document supplies inventory coverage rather than that verdict.
